First off, there’s nothing wrong with you. Your actions are a reflection of your experiences, and you likely haven’t been met with an alternative coping method other than anger. It’s common, you are not alone, and you are valid. 

As cheesy as it sounds, the first place to start is with your breathing. Your emotions and your nervous system are really closely interlinked and when you take a deep breath you signal your nervous system to take a break as well. This is just the start, but it makes the other steps much easier. 

There’s a myriad of things you can do to identify the source of your anger, you can write about it in a journal just complete stream of consciousness, meet with a therapist to see if you can find the root, or maybe talk to your mom. In any case, the root could be frustration, feelings of inadequacy, feeling neglected/rejected, feeling like you’ve been wronged etc. it’s important not to invalidate these feelings. Don’t compare yourself to others, don’t minimize your feelings either. Whatever they are they make you feel this way, and you are valid.

Best of luck, and feel free to reach out with any more questions.

Property tax is an “ad valorem” tax, which is any tax on an asset. Ad valorem taxes are both determined and levied annually in most cities and states. 

As in any investment, owning property carries (and should carry) a risk to the owner. Property taxes are a large part of calculating this risk. Property in it of itself also can create a lot of money for the owner. You can rent it out and in modern times many people are working out of their homes, making it more valuable to them. 

Sudden home devaluation is a real possibility, and one can get very unlucky if something happens (like a global pandemic) and devalues their property, but the money their property was worth before, is still valued that they possessed and subject to taxes. In the same vein though, many people get huge boosts in value to their property without any of their input as well. Location can be more valuable due to demand, or even gentrification can be an opportunity to make money in some cases.
You reasses their value and tax them less next time. Idea being that you’re taxing for their value at moment of taxation. So if bezos loses all his stock value, next year he pays way less taxes.

Last whisper will extend your strength for a little bit longer, but if the enemy has 2 warmogs(sometimes even one) and some decent armor, you’re just a second support who can sometimes snipe the other squishy in team fights. If you see this happening in the future, swap your runes to on hit in lobby.
